```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```

```{r setup}
library(transmap)
data(transmap_example)
Y <- transmap_example$Y
data_list <- list(Z = transmap_example$z, N = transmap_example$n)
prog <- r_transcca(data_list, K = 2, sumabs = 0.25)
```

`transmap_global()` turns the gene loadings of global programs into program
phenotypes. For expression $Y$ (samples $\times$ genes) and gene loadings $V$
(genes $\times$ programs), the phenotypes are

$$S = Y V,$$

that is, for each sample, the expression of each program's genes weighted by
their loadings. Genes with zero loading do not contribute.

# 1. Build phenotypes from transCCA programs

```{r global}
glob <- transmap_global(Y, prog)
names(glob)
dim(glob$scores)
head(round(glob$scores, 3), 3)
```

The result holds

- `scores`: samples $\times$ programs matrix of program phenotypes;
- `loadings`: the gene loadings restricted to the genes used;
- `genes_used` and `genes_missing`: program genes present in and absent from
  `Y`.

# 2. Covariates and scaling

With `covariates`, covariates and an intercept are regressed out of the
expression before scoring. Only samples shared by `Y` and `covariates` are
kept.

```{r covariates}
glob_adj <- transmap_global(Y, prog, covariates = transmap_example$covariates)
dim(glob_adj$scores)
```

With `scale = TRUE`, each gene is standardized first, so that genes contribute
according to their loadings rather than their expression variance:

```{r scale}
glob_std <- transmap_global(Y, prog, scale = TRUE)
round(apply(glob_std$scores, 2, sd), 3)
```

# 3. Programs learned from another data set

Programs can be learned from the association statistics of one set of samples
and scored in the expression data of another (for example, an independent
split of the cohort, another cohort or another cell type). Genes in the
program that are missing from `Y` are ignored and reported:

```{r missing}
Y_sub <- Y[, setdiff(colnames(Y), c("GENE03", "GENE26"))]
glob_sub <- transmap_global(Y_sub, prog)
glob_sub$genes_missing
```

# 4. Custom loadings

A plain genes $\times$ programs loading matrix with gene row names can be used
instead of an `r_transcca()` result, for example only the programs that pass
null testing (see [Null Testing of Global Programs](Global_Program_Null_Testing.html)),
or programs from other methods:

```{r custom}
V_one <- prog$V[, "Program_1", drop = FALSE]
glob_one <- transmap_global(Y, V_one)
colnames(glob_one$scores)
```

# 5. Global and local phenotypes

Local phenotypes summarize co-expression modules, without genotype
information. Global phenotypes summarize genes chosen because they share
*trans* associations with the same variants. The two scales are complementary
and can be mapped together:

```{r combine}
hs <- r_hotspot(Y, min_gene = 5)
loc <- transmap_local(Y, hs, null_z = transmap_example$null_z)
pheno <- cbind(loc$scores, glob$scores)
dim(pheno)
```

See [Trans-QTL Mapping with Program Phenotypes](Trans_QTL_Mapping_with_Programs.html)
for how to use these phenotypes.
